topics.topic: `read_spooled_file` handling of caller-supplied digest/size/media_type mismatches (ignore descriptive fields vs refuse)
questions: If caller supplies digest/size/media_type that do not match the located SpooledFile record, should the operation ignore them or refuse?
If caller supplies digest/size/media_type that do not match the located SpooledFile record (while lookup identity matches), must the operation ignore those fields or refuse?
When caller-supplied digest/size/media_type disagree with stored SpooledFile facts but lookup identity matches, must the operation refuse, or ignore those descriptive fields and return bytes?

judgement.why: The text explicitly says lookup is by identity and digest/size/media_type are descriptive only.

topics.topic: `get_repair_view` continuation token binding/validity scope across slot and other selectors
questions: Is the continuation token also bound to the same slot_id (and other request selectors), and what refusal applies if reused with a different slot?

If that continuation token is later used with a different slot id or with changed paging parameters beyond size, must the call be refused, or silently continue using the token-embedded slot/set context?

judgement.divergence: Behavior A: `get_repair_view` binds continuation tokens to the original `slot_id` (and other selectors) and refuses reuse with a different slot as `invalid_request`; Behavior B: it accepts the token with a different `slot_id` and pages NodeExecutions using the token-embedded implementation set while re-reading other parts for the new request. The owner or agent caller notices refusal vs returned data scope.
judgement.why: The text defines token-carried implementation-set paging for `get_repair_view` but does not state whether cross-slot reuse must be refused or accepted.

topics.topic: Behavior when a non-read manifest declares idempotency_key = null (refuse send vs allow unkeyed send)
questions: For a non-`read` operation whose manifest `idempotency_key` is `null`, must send be refused, or allowed with no key recorded?

topics.topic: Whether refusals/internal_error guarantee no writes, including `stop_required` paths

What guarantee should callers attach to MCP `internal_error`: does it always mean the failing change wrote nothing, or can it also mean a `stop_required` path where a record was written?
